messages:
elaine: Heads up — SAST is auto-suppressing a cluster of findings from the new 'quiet-finder' rule across infra/services/auth. Looks like some high-severity SQLi hits are being marked as noise. Need triage.

sec-scan-bot: Automated: 5 findings suppressed by policy quiet-finder v1.2 for infra/services/auth. Suppression reason: \"pattern match low confidence\". Report: https://scans.internal/5212 

michael: That sounds bad. Can you paste one of the suppressed finding payloads?

elaine: here's one (redacted):
```
scanner: sastd
id: SF-99811
file: auth/login.go:142
finding: possible SQL injection via fmt.Sprintf -> query
policy: quiet-finder v1.2 (auto-suppress)
evidence: redacted
```

jordan: I pulled the raw artifact for SF-99811 and the scanner attempted to fetch keystore proof but got a 403. Guessing the suppression happened because the scanner couldn't fetch runtime constants. Error from the fetch: 
```
HTTP 403 from https://keystore.internal/kms/decrypt
request_id: abc123
principal: svc-scan-old
```

ash: We rotated svc-scan service account yesterday; sounds like the scanner didn't pick up the new principal. KMS policy still lists svc-scan-read but token exchange for the scanner agent failed. I'll grep audit logs.

michael: If KMS prevented decrypt, we must treat suppression cautiously. Either unsuppress and re-run or attach KMS audit proof to justify a suppression. Suppression without audit = no-go for high severity.

ash: Found audit lines: 
```
2026-03-20T02:11:04Z KMS Decrypt DENIED principal=svc-scan-old method=Decrypt request_id=abc123
2026-03-20T02:11:05Z KMS Decrypt ALLOW principal=svc-scan-v2 method=Decrypt request_id=abc124
```

elaine: OK — action plan: unsuppress SF-99811, re-run the scan once keystore access is fixed, and open an RBAC PR to ensure svc-scan-v2 has stable permissions. Who will own the RBAC PR?

jordan: I can own the RBAC PR and the scan ticket. I'll attach the KMS audit IDs to the ticket (SEC-321) and include the deny/allow lines.

michael: Please also add a short playbook entry to SEC-OPS: if scanner gets repeated 403s when fetching keystore, auto-open an infra incident and create a temp grant for svc-scan so scans don't silently suppress.

ash: Granting temporary decrypt to svc-scan-v2 for 1 hour and will post evidence here. Doing it now :hammer_and_wrench: 

sec-scan-bot: Action: Unsuppress SF-99811 — un-suppression requested by elaine. Created scan-run 5212346802.

jordan: Re-run completed and the finding is now visible with stack trace. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/auth/pull/789 — assigning @michael for review :eyes: 

michael: Reviewing the PR. If it's a real SQLi I'll file a remediation ticket and we should add a unit test that asserts the query path uses parameterized queries. Also will add a rule tweak so quiet-finder doesn't auto-suppress cases where keystore fetch failed.

elaine: Thanks all. We'll close the loop once the PR merges and the RBAC change is merged. Short postmortem note in security-ops will capture the root cause (SA rotation + missing scanner propagation).
